newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower, volumes light.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower, volumes light.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly lower again Monday, although volume was light and the lack of follow through to Friday's selling suggested there may not be much more downside left in the move, traders said.

"It looks to be just light fund selling pushing precious metals down, with people disappointed the complex hasn't benefitted more from the weakness in equities recently, but open interest is very low, so it may not mean much," one bullion banker said.
COMEX June gold ended down $0.60 at $348.70 an ounce after trading from $349.80 to $348.50.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $346.00/50 compared to the London afternoon fix of $346.75 and the New York close Friday around $346.60/$347.10.
Daily momentum indicators have a slightly negative tone, but volatility measures are still subsiding, analysts said.
Open interest in COMEX gold rose 2,617 lots to 151,621 contracts on Friday's downmove, but is still near its lowest levels for a year.

"In the absence of heavy selling and increased volatility, we may find the option market takes over again and we remain locked within this ($345.00-355.00) range for the rest of the year," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said.

CFTC's Commitments of Traders data, reported late Friday, showed funds maintained their net short positions in COMEX gold over the two weeks ended April 8, though the position was still smaller than the record net short position seen in late 1996.
As of April 8, "non-commercial" or fund net short positions stood at 8,863 contracts.

Indian gold prices slipped slightly Monday, after rising last week, when an air traffic controllers strike disrupted imports, but demand was expected to pick up again seasonally for the April-May second wedding season.
Gold and silver equities slid lower again Monday also, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's index of North American gold and silver stocks slipping to 99.20 near the close, a new two year low.
COMEX May silver ended up 0.3 cent at $4.725 after slumping Friday back down toward the contract low of $4.655 set last Thursday.
Open interest in COMEX silver fell 573 lots Friday to 98,756 contracts, with funds believed to be liquidating remaining long positions.
Funds remained net long in silver according to the latest CFTC data, but the net long position was down to only 3,258 contracts as of April 8, from 24,456 two weeks earlier.
Spot silver was quoted at $4.73/75, not far from the three-month low of $4.70 posted last week.
NYMEX July platinum ended down $2.70 at $370.10, while the October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread slipped back to $17.60 an ounce from a three-week high of $20.40 Friday.
NYMEX June palladium lost $0.80 to $154.00, with the market expecting talks to resume on a Russia/Japan supply contract this week.

Russian palladium supplies to Japan have been disrupted since last December due to Russian fiscal and administrative problems, and as Russia supplies 60 percent of the world's palladium, prices are up about 25 percent on year-end 1996 levels.
Short-term palladium lease rates were reported around 10 to 13 percent Monday, with six-month rates around 2.5 percent.
Last week, Swiss and Japanese trade house were forced to borrow metal on the spot market to cover sales made in arbitrage trades with Europe and America, traders said.
"Theoretically this is all very bullish for platinum and palladium," Arnold said.
"We have lost four months of sales and the Russians are known to have called in platinum and palladium out on loan to the market," he said.
In the meantime, funds were maintaining net long positions in platinum and palladium, the CFTC data for the two weeks ended April 8 showed.
